claims.claim: The name 'tomorrow' comes from a very old story.
claims.note: The word 'tomorrow' comes from Old English etymology, not a story.

claims.claim: People noticed that the days kept going around the sun and decided to give names to the days of the week.
claims.note: Days do not go around the sun, Earth orbits the sun, and 'tomorrow' is not a day of the week.

claims.claim: They decided to call the day right after today 'tomorrow' because it was the next day they would see the sun rise again.
claims.note: This etymology is completely fabricated; 'tomorrow' actually derives from old Germanic terms meaning 'on the morning'.

claims.claim: Your heart is a pump that circulates blood throughout your entire body.
It carries oxygen and nutrients to your organs.
It keeps your muscles strong.
It helps regulate your breathing and temperature.
claims.note: While blood circulation contributes to temperature regulation, breathing is primarily regulated by the brainstem and respiratory centers, not the heart itself.

claims.claim: Your favorite toy car moves because of a motor inside it.
claims.note: Not all toy cars have motors; some are pulled, pushed, or use friction, but it is an acceptable simplification for an example of how things work.

claims.claim: Plants make their own food using sunlight.
claims.note: Plants actually use sunlight to convert carbon dioxide and water into food through photosynthesis, but this is an acceptable simplification for a child.

claims.claim: Months get their lengths from the Earth's orbit around the Sun, which isn't a perfect circle but an ellipse.
claims.note: Month lengths are based on historical calendar design and the Moon's phases/Earth's solar year, not the eccentricity of Earth's orbit.

claims.claim: As the Earth moves further away from or closer to the Sun during its orbit, it takes slightly more or less time to complete a full rotation on its axis.
claims.note: Earth's rotational speed on its axis does not change because of its distance from the Sun.

claims.claim: To compensate for this, we add extra days to February and stretch out the other months.
claims.note: Days are not added to February to compensate for changing rotational speed.

claims.claim: The extra day in February is added because the Earth actually completes one full rotation relative to the stars (a sidereal day) every 24 hours, while our calendar day is based on the solar day.
claims.note: A sidereal day is about 23 hours and 56 minutes, and leap years are added to account for the fractional extra day in Earth's 365.25-day solar year, not sidereal versus solar day differences.

claims.claim: Electric cars are special cars that run on electricity instead of gas
They use a big battery to store energy
They spin a motor to turn the wheels
They are much better for the environment because they don't make any pollution
Planes fly in the sky because they have powerful engines.
Inside the engine, there is a special machine called a jet turbine that spins really fast.
This spinning creates a huge amount of air movement, kind of like a giant fan.
The plane's wings are shaped just right to catch this moving air and push it down.
claims.note: Wings generate lift from the forward motion of the plane moving through still air, not primarily from catching air blown backward by the engine.

claims.claim: That creates lift, which helps the plane stay up in the air instead of falling down.
The biggest planet in our solar system is Jupiter.
Jupiter is so big that if you stacked up all the other planets on top of each other, Jupiter would still be way too small to touch the sky.
claims.note: Stacking planets on top of each other does not make sense in terms of reaching the sky, and all other planets combined actually fit inside the volume of Jupiter.

claims.claim: The beat is like the sound of the referee's whistle, telling everyone when to run and stop.
claims.note: A beat in music is a steady, continuous pulse, not a whistle that tells people when to start and stop.

claims.claim: Rhythm is how you move your body while running, like stomping your feet or jumping up and down.
claims.note: While body movement can have rhythm, this is a metaphorical explanation rather than a definition of musical rhythm.

claims.claim: The beat is what keeps everything going, and the rhythm is how you make it fun and exciting.
claims.note: This is a vague, child-friendly analogy rather than a precise musical distinction.

claims.claim: Trains are designed to be long because they need a lot of space to carry heavy loads efficiently.
A standard freight train can haul around 200 cars.
Each freight train car weighs several hundred tons.
claims.note: A typical freight car weighs around 25 to 30 tons empty and up to 100 to 140 tons fully loaded, not several hundred tons per car.

claims.claim: An axle is a powerful set of wheels.
claims.note: An axle is simply a central shaft for a rotating wheel or gear, not a powerful set of wheels.

claims.claim: The extra length allows trains to stop safely on steep grades without derailing.
claims.note: Train length does not inherently help stop safely on steep grades; in fact, longer trains can make braking more complex and require distributed power.

claims.claim: Longer trains mean lower per-car fuel consumption.
A pumpkin is usually orange
A pumpkin gets its orange color from the orange flesh inside
claims.note: A pumpkin's exterior color comes from its skin/rind, and the color is due to pigments like carotenoids, not simply because the flesh inside is orange.

claims.claim: Singing in the shower helps release endorphins
Endorphins are chemicals in your brain that make you feel good
Singing in the shower is a great way to bond with friends or family while you're washing up
Berries give our bodies energy.
Berries help us grow big and strong.
Ancient Romans originally celebrated the start of the new year around February 15th, based on their lunar calendar.
claims.note: The Roman republican calendar originally started the year in March, not February 15th.

claims.claim: Julius Caesar introduced the Julian calendar in 45 BCE.
Julius Caesar's introduction of the Julian calendar shifted the start of the year to January 1st.
Ice floats because it is made of water
claims.note: Being made of water is not a sufficient explanation for floating, since liquid water does not float on liquid water.

claims.claim: At 0°C (32°F), water turns into its solid form, which we call ice
Ice has a lower density than liquid water
For the same volume, ice takes up more space, making it lighter than the liquid water it was frozen from
When you drop a piece of ice into a glass of water, it displaces the water, creating a buoyant force that keeps it floating on top
Using public transportation, carpooling, or biking instead of driving alone reduces your carbon footprint.
Turning off lights when you leave a room helps reduce your carbon footprint.
Limiting the use of single-use plastics helps reduce your carbon footprint.
Buying products with minimal packaging helps reduce your carbon footprint.
Choosing energy-efficient appliances at home is a huge step in reducing your carbon footprint.
A banana tastes sweet.
A banana is yellow when it is ripe.
A banana is green when it is not ripe.
The balloon was filled with air.
claims.note: A balloon filled only with ordinary breath (air) will not float up into the sky; it needs a lighter gas like helium or hot air.

claims.claim: The balloon went up high up in the sky when he let it go.
claims.note: An air-filled balloon will fall to the ground, not float up into the sky.

claims.claim: Friends make us feel happy because they care about us, listen when we have a story to tell, and share fun games and adventures together.
When you laugh or play with your friends, your brain releases special chemicals called endorphins that make you feel good and relaxed.
Having a budget helps you manage your money wisely.
A budget gives you a clear picture of how much you earn and spend each month.
A budget helps you avoid overspending.
A budget helps you save for big goals like a car or college.
A budget helps you pay off debt.
Budgeting teaches you about financial responsibility and planning for the future.
Being afraid of the dark is called 'scotophobia.'
claims.note: The clinical term for a persistent and abnormal fear of the dark is nyctophobia, not scotophobia.

claims.claim: Our brains are wired to protect us.
When we are alone in the dark, our brain thinks there might be something lurking around the corner.
As you grow older, your brain learns to process fear differently.
You usually get used to feeling safe in the dark as you grow older.
Galaxies are mostly made up of gas, dust, and dark matter.
The gas and dust form giant clouds that glow brightly in infrared light.
Dark matter acts like a cosmic scaffold holding everything together.
Stars are the main building blocks of galaxies.
The gravitational pull of all those stars keeps the entire structure stable over billions of years.
claims.note: The gravitational pull of stars alone is not what keeps galaxies stable; dark matter provides the vast majority of the gravitational mass needed to hold galaxies together.

claims.claim: When you mix blue and yellow together, you get green.
Flowers come in lots of colors, like red, yellow, and blue.
Some flowers make yummy food for animals.
Some flowers smell nice.
Food becomes spicy because it contains compounds called capsaicinoids
Capsaicinoids are found in the seeds, skin, and white pith of chili peppers
When these compounds touch your tongue, they trigger tiny sensors that send signals to your brain telling you that something is hot
Different types of peppers have different levels of heat, measured in Scoville units
Allergies happen when your immune system mistakes harmless things like pollen, dust, or certain foods for invaders.
Allergies happen when your immune system sends out too many protective chemicals.
If you are genetically predisposed to allergies, your immune system is more likely to react this way.
Butterflies fly to find food
They eat flowers for yummy nectar
Day and night happen because our Earth is spinning.
When you stop and spin the other way, it's nighttime.
claims.note: The Earth does not stop and spin the other way to create night; it continues rotating in the same direction.

claims.claim: The whole planet spins, and that's why we get day and night every single day.
Rainbows happen because of raindrops.
Raindrops catch the sunshine.
Raindrops act like little prisms.
Raindrops break the light into all the colors of the rainbow.
Yucky smells can happen when food gets old
Yucky smells can happen when food is cooked in metal pans
claims.note: Cooking food in metal pans does not inherently cause yucky smells.

claims.claim: Air can get trapped inside a closed container, like a jar of peanut butter, which makes it smell funny
claims.note: Trapped air in a closed container does not inherently cause a funny smell; smells are caused by volatile molecules from the food itself.
